items.narrative:
The audit covers 761 traceability events recorded between 2025-01-03 and 2025-09-23, spanning 551 shipping events, 145 transformation events, 64 first land-based receiving events, and 1 receiving event. All 32 products in scope fall into the definite-on tier of the Food Traceability List, meaning every transaction in this dataset carries full traceability obligations. The business transacts with 29 external trading partners, all of whom are banded at the A level, and logged 216 internal transfer events during the period.

Five findings are rated high severity and ten are rated medium, for a total of 15 findings. The most pressing issues are: 41 lots flagged for duplicate traceability lot codes requiring review, which undermines the ability to uniquely identify and trace product; 354 key data elements missing out of 6,785 graded, yielding a KDE coverage rate of 0.9478 that must reach completeness before any regulatory submission; 6 backward-lineage records and 1 transformation-linkage record that need review, meaning the chain of custody cannot be fully reconstructed for those lots; and 1 mass-balance and 1 date-ordering anomaly that suggest either data-entry errors or genuine product-flow irregularities. Additionally, 2 products—04598767000211 and 04598767000495—are declared as General products in the system yet are classified as definite-on under the Food Traceability List, a mismatch that creates compliance exposure if those records are presented to regulators as-is. Two scope-or-exemption-uncertainty findings and a traceability-plan finding round out the high-priority work.

Begin immediately by resolving the 41 duplicate traceability lot codes, as this is the single largest data-integrity problem in the dataset. Simultaneously, correct the product-category declarations for 04598767000211 and 04598767000495 so they reflect their definite-on status throughout all records. Work through the 354 missing KDEs systematically by CTE, prioritizing the shipping and transformation sheets given their event volumes of 551 and 145 respectively. The 6 backward-lineage records, 1 transformation-linkage record, 1 mass-balance record, and 1 date-ordering record should each be investigated with the relevant lot documentation to determine whether the root cause is a data-entry error or an actual gap in physical traceability. Finally, finalize and formalize the traceability plan document, as its absence is itself a finding and is a prerequisite for demonstrating readiness to regulators.
